readme:
# Made-in-China Scraper - Chinese Manufacturer & Supplier Directory

Scrape supplier data from [Made-in-China.com](https://www.made-in-china.com), one of the world's largest B2B platforms connecting global buyers with Chinese manufacturers and suppliers.

## What data do you get?

For each supplier, the scraper extracts:

- **Company name** and description
- **Business type** (Manufacturer/Factory, Trading Company, etc.)
- **Main products** list
- **Full address** (street, city, province)
- **Employee count** and annual revenue
- **Factory size** (plant area in square meters)
- **Certifications** (ISO, CE, FCC, RoHS, etc.)
- **Quality management system**
- **Export markets** and trade capacity
- **Company logo**
- **Year founded**

## Use with AI Agents (MCP)

Connect this actor to any MCP-compatible AI client: Claude Desktop, Claude.ai, Cursor, VS Code, LangChain, LlamaIndex, or custom agents.

**Apify MCP server URL:**

```
https://mcp.apify.com?tools=santamaria-automations/made-in-china-scraper
```

**Example prompt once connected:**

> "Use `made-in-china-scraper` to scrape company data from made in china. Return results as a table."

Clients that support dynamic tool discovery (Claude.ai, VS Code) will receive the full input schema automatically via `add-actor`.

## How to use

### Option 1: Paste a search URL

1. Go to [made-in-china.com](https://www.made-in-china.com)
2. Search for suppliers using the "Suppliers" tab
3. Copy the search results URL
4. Paste it into the **Search URLs** field

### Option 2: Use search query

Set the **Search Query** (e.g., "solar panel", "led light", "electronics") field. The scraper builds the URL automatically.

### Input example

```json
{
  "searchUrls": ["https://www.made-in-china.com/manufacturers/electronics.html"],
  "maxResults": 50,
  "includeDetails": true
}
```

### Input parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `searchUrls` | array | Made-in-China.com search result URLs. A plain keyword in this list is searched as a keyword |
| `searchQuery` | string | Search keyword to build URL automatically |
| `maxResults` | integer | Maximum number of suppliers (default: 100; 10 when no searchUrls or searchQuery is given (demo run)) |
| `includeDetails` | boolean | Fetch profile pages for full data (default: true) |

## Contact fields

With `includeDetails` on, each supplier's public contact page is also read.

| Field | Status |
|-------|--------|
| `contact_person`, `contact_title`, `contact_department` | Filled when the supplier shows a contact on its public page |
| `website` | The supplier's own website, taken from Made-in-China's public "Website" link (null if the supplier lists none) |
| `phone`, `email` | Always null. Made-in-China only shows these to signed-in buyers, so this actor does not return them |

Rows where the detail pages added nothing beyond the search card are billed as SERP results, not detail results.

## Performance

- ~30 suppliers per SERP page
- With details: about 3 to 5 seconds per supplier (profile and contact pages, rate limited)
- SERP only: ~30 suppliers per second
- Memory: 128 MB (Go binary, ~12MB Docker image)

## Run time and status messages

- A run that would pass its run timeout stops shortly before it, saves what it has and ends with the number of suppliers delivered. For large lists use a longer run timeout or a lower `maxResults`, or turn `includeDetails` off.
- A run that finds nothing ends successfully with a plain reason in the status message (empty search, search page not found, or the site refusing every connection level tried) and no charge. If the account plan lacks the connection groups the site needs, the status says so.
- A search page that loads but cannot be read (layout change) ends as failed with the reason in the status message.

## Data protection

This actor returns only data that is publicly visible on the source pages. Results can include personal data, such as names, phone numbers, email addresses and addresses of private persons, sole traders or contact persons. Where the source labels an entry type, it is included so you can filter the results yourself.

You are responsible for using the data lawfully, including the GDPR/DSGVO, national data-protection laws and unfair-competition rules (e.g. UWG) for marketing and outreach.
